source_identity.original_source_statement_tex:
\label{proposition-Noetherian-adic-constructible}
Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme. Let $\Lambda$ be a Noetherian ring and
let $I \subset \Lambda$ be an ideal. Let $K$ be an object of
$D_{cons}(X, \Lambda)$. Then $K$ is adic constructible
(Definition \ref{definition-adic-constructible}).

stage_b_reviewed_content.statement:
**Source terminology (not an added hypothesis).** A constructible proétale $\Lambda$-module sheaf ($\Lambda$ Noetherian) is finite-type locally constant on a finite constructible locally closed stratification of each affine open. $D_{cons}(X,\Lambda)$ consists of derived $I$-complete $\Lambda$-complexes with mod-$I$ constructible cohomology and locally finite Tor dimension. In the derived sense, adic lisse means locally a finite complex of completed finite projective $\Lambda^\wedge$-modules, and adic constructible means finite locally closed strata with that property.

Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme. Let $\Lambda$ be a Noetherian ring and
let $I \subset \Lambda$ be an ideal. Let $K$ be an object of
$D_{cons}(X, \Lambda)$. Then $K$ is adic constructible
(Definition \ref{definition-adic-constructible}).
